_note: Explicit mapping from real-world metrics to simulation variables. A proxy is never silently treated as the real variable: every proxy mapping must state its limitations, and the registry refuses to load one that does not.

mappings.source_metric: Average delay for LATE vessel arrivals (Sea-Intelligence Global Liner Performance)
mappings.rationale: The simulation variable shipping_delay is 'average additional door-to-door transit time for cargo routed through the affected corridor', in days. Sea-Intelligence publishes an average delay for late vessel arrivals in days, which is the closest publicly available quantity in the same unit — no conversion is required, so the mapping itself introduces no scaling error.
mappings.limitations: THREE material limitations, all of which weaken the replay: (1) GEOGRAPHY — the published figure is a GLOBAL aggregate across all trades, while the simulated world is a single port. A one-port disruption can only ever move a small share of a global average, so the model and the observation are not measuring the same population. (2) FREQUENCY — the series is MONTHLY while the simulation runs WEEKLY, so a four-and-a-half week disruption is spanned by roughly two observations. (3) CONFOUNDING — mid-2021 global container shipping was under severe pandemic-driven congestion from many simultaneous causes; movement in this series cannot be attributed to Yantian. Consequence: this proxy can test DIRECTION weakly and cannot test MAGNITUDE at all.

mappings.source_metric: Reported terminal operating capacity as a share of normal (carrier advisories and trade press)
mappings.rationale: port_capacity is defined as an index where 100 = normal weekly throughput, so a reported '30% of normal capacity' maps to 30 index points by construction. This mapping is used to define the INJECTED EVENT, not to evaluate the model: it is a model input, not a test of it.
mappings.limitations: Reported operating capacity is an operational statement by carriers and press, not a measured throughput figure. The transition dates between capacity levels are known only approximately (last week of May; partial reopening 10 June; full resumption 24 June), so the injected event's step boundaries carry date uncertainty of a few days. No weekly TEU throughput series was obtainable to check these percentages.

mappings.source_metric: Container volume awaiting export at the affected terminal (TEU)
mappings.rationale: Containers stranded awaiting export are the most directly observable counterpart to the model's order_backlog.
mappings.limitations: NOT USABLE AS A SERIES, and therefore not scored. Only isolated point estimates exist ('more than 400,000 TEU' on 14 June 2021; '~300,000 TEU' reported elsewhere), they are lower bounds rather than measurements, and no normal-conditions baseline TEU figure was obtainable — so there is no way to convert them to the model's 100 = normal index without inventing the denominator. Recorded here to make the gap explicit rather than to enable a fit.
